subject: Rajiv Gandhi
guidance: Four career phases; ten gender dimensions and ten era dimensions per phase. Separate personal and party elections, policy stages, commission findings and criminal procedures. Field-level review is not certification of every neighbouring cell. Open evidence gaps remain explicit.

rows.Finding / value: Rajiv Gandhi (20 August 1944–21 May 1991), Congress(I) leader and Prime Minister of India; born in Bombay, assassinated at Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu.
rows.Corroboration: See field evidence and source limitations

rows.Finding / value: 31 October 1984–2 December 1989: one continuous spell, with a new ministry after the December 1984 general election.
Son of Indira and Feroze Gandhi, grandson of Jawaharlal Nehru. An airline pilot before politics, he entered after brother Sanjay’s death and won Amethi in 1981.
Attended Doon School, Trinity College Cambridge and Imperial College London. These accounts establish study, not a completed university degree.
rows.Research note: No original education credential inspected; do not describe him as an engineering graduate.

rows.Finding / value: Four Amethi victories: 1981 by-election and 1984, 1989, 1991 general elections. The last result was posthumous; he did not serve in the tenth Lok Sabha.
ECI reports Congress winning 404 seats in 1984 and 197 in 1989. Rajiv retained Amethi when his government lost power; party totals are separate from his personal results.
Telecom development, education institutions, anti-defection legislation and a lower voting age marked the period. Institutional origins, enactment and later outcomes are distinguished.
Panagariya stresses partial liberalisation and fiscal fragility; Rodrik and Subramanian emphasise an earlier pro-business shift. Neither account makes Rajiv the sole origin of faster growth.
Negotiations produced accords in Punjab, Assam and Mizoram. Their trajectories differed: agreement did not bring immediate peace in Punjab or resolve Assam’s immigration disputes.
